Done: the next batch is three briefs, led by a fix for the bug that cut the last batch. Committed and pushed as 8b0d81e4.

**Why the batch was cut:** b1024 finished (ac8a38a6, `Fixes #1024`), but its report named a new defect. A lambda that a callee keeps can capture a `String` parameter; if the parameter is not used after the call, rustc rejects the program with "Lifetime may not live long enough" instead of Nikaia handling it. I reproduced it on the current build, with a free function and with a trait method. Two control cases behave correctly: a local `String` in the same place runs, and using the parameter after the call gets `NK2101`. The cause is in `tools/keeps.nika` (`keeps_blocks_in`): it treats a lambda's body as running during the call, even when the callee keeps the lambda. `spawn` already handles this case correctly and is the model for the fix.

**Issue filed:** #1025, label `ready`, written as a brief. I ran all three of its test cases before writing it.

**Batch** (`docs/briefs/batch.txt`, in order):
1. `b1025-kept-lambda-names.md`: builder, Opus, 80 turns, $20; `Fixes #1025`. It may edit only `keeps.nika`, its lowered file, `contracts/keeps.rs` and the new tests.
2. `b1012b-trait-column-refusals.md`: unchanged; it did not run last time. Its precondition (#1024) is now on `develop`.
3. `b1012c-trait-column-data.md`: stops on its own if b1012b is not on `develop`.

**CI:** passed up to b2866e02; the runs for 0d053671 to a3ec9600 had not finished when I checked.

**Repository changes:** the new brief, `batch.txt`, a new entry in the State section of `docs/architect.md`, and the report at `docs/briefs/architect-task.md.report.md`.

**Owed:** the supervisor still owes the version raise for #1024; the Changelog line is in its report. Older items are listed in the State section.

**Needs from the main session / owner:** nothing.
